articles.title: Rockstar North Boss Knew Some GTA 6 Players Would 'Reject' New Systems Like Criminal Profiles, but Insists 'You Can Still Do Whatever You Wanted to Do Before'
articles.summary: Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson knew some GTA 6 players would "reject" new systems like criminal profiles, but insisted "you can still do whatever you wanted to do before."
articles.body:
GTA 6 is by far the furthest Rockstar has pushed one of its games on a gameplay level. Perhaps nothing showcases that more than the criminal profile system ticking away in the background at all times, judging the way you act in its world as Jason and Lucia. No longer is Grand Theft Auto a sandbox where hedonism is widely encouraged, but a place that judges you for partaking in it.

It’s a system that has caused much debate within the player base, with some feeling as if they’re being punished for how they traditionally played GTA games. It was something that Rockstar admitted to have been a little worried about when YouTuber TGG visited the studio months ago and claimed it was "going to change GTA."

"I thought, 'Oh s**t, we’re in trouble,'" Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson told VGC . “But I said, 'It doesn’t change everything; it changes what GTA can be.' So for us, I think it opens a new range of choices and decisions for the player to make. You can still do whatever you wanted to do before, but now you have other options."

The criminal profile system reacts to how violently you choose to act throughout GTA 6’s open world and missions. Opt for headshot kills over debilitating kneecaps? You’ll move away from the "professional" end of the spectrum towards "psycho" and eventually "irredeemable." From experience, though, I can confirm that it takes quite the effort to reach that point on the scale after going on one murderous rampage after the next.

Which criminal profile you land on by the end of Jason and Lucia’s story will factor into which ending you get, but for the most part, it’s not something that necessarily needs to be playing on your mind at all times. My characters were considered “professional” at the end of my playthrough, and, believe me, I spilt my fair share of blood along the way.

Nelson appears to know that not all players will necessarily be on board with changes to the GTA formula like this, though, and expects some to "reject this new stuff we’re offering." He does hope it may help to make people think differently about how they approach Rockstar games in a post-Red Dead Redemption 2 world, though.

"I hope it changes the way players who want to engage with it play the game," Nelson continued to tell VGC. "In GTA 5 you started with a bank robbery in North Yankton, and you’re murdering like 40 cops off the rip, and you’re setting these guys up as what they are. We were conscious of that.

"Lucia takes the bullets out of the gun at the start of the game. She goes in, and it’s not like you can kill a bunch of people. So we wanted to start them off with a bit less baggage. They’re trying to make a go of this semi-legitimate life. When you pick up with Jason, he’s still a criminal; he’s still getting in trouble with Donnie and all that, but he’s sort of been living this relatively criminal-adjacent existence."

Whether GTA 6 feels like "classic GTA" or not is certainly a conversation to be had, but there’s no denying that the opening hours of Rockstar’s latest connects you to its characters more convincingly than the series has done in the past. Are you a fan of the criminal profile system? Let us know in the comments.

We’ve got the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide here on IGN, complete with comprehensive walkthroughs up to Chapter 5 , guides for the Optional Missions and Illegal Operations you’ll find in Leonida, and much more. Just getting started in Chapter 1 ? Check out our Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , and make a note of the Best Free Weapons to Find Early . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: Someone Is Making One of Baldur's Gate 3's Most Popular Villains Romanceable
articles.summary: One of Baldur's Gate 3's main villains, Gortash, could be romanceable soon thanks to this new fan-made mod.
articles.body:
Baldur's Gate 3 has no shortage of romances and romantic encounters, but not everyone in Faerûn is up for a smooch.

When developer Larian was still rolling out updates, fans would often ask for more romances to be added, whether it be for Jaheira or Rolan, but it was never meant to be.

One of the most popular requests was actually for one of Baldur's Gate 3's main villains, Gortash. Larian was very much aware of this, and actually addressed these fans in the patch notes in 2024.

"Listen, he’s a complicated guy who’s busy contemplating the minutia of death cult office politics," Larian said at the time. "Babygurl doesn’t have time to kiss."

But now, a fan is stepping up, adding the Gortash romance that so many were asking for. TikTok user Equipouet has shared some clips from the mod, which is still a work in progress. It shows the player character being invited to spend time with Gortash, played by Lucius Malfoy actor Jason Isaacs, after his coronation in Act 3, all with new dialogue and animations.

We're told that we'll be able to make our own choices when we meet Gortash, specifically whether we want to "charm him, keep him guessing, or walk away." So, if you really hate Gortash, you could also use the mod to let him down.

Much more is teased for the mod, like a ball held by Gortash, letters to exchange with him, and "choices with consequences." There will also be changes to how the story plays out if your character is The Dark Urge, since it's in your backstory that you already have a history with Gortash.

The mod is still being worked on, but the author says they will submit it for console release approval once it's done. That process can be lengthy, however, and there's no guarantee that it will pass the approval stage, especially if it's too bulky for console.

In the meantime, Gortash kissers will keep having to use their imagination. Like us would-be Jaheira kissers. There are also plenty of other mods to try out, including a bunch that have Larian's seal of approval and can be installed within the game's own mod manager.

Rhiannon (she/her) is a freelance journalist who has been in the industry since 2019. She won MCV's Women in Games award in 2025 and adores RPGs. You can follow her on Bluesky at @rhithewitch.

articles.title: Tech layoffs tracker 2026: All the job losses across Disney, Intel, Amazon, Microsoft, Apple, Meta and others
articles.summary: There are only a few weeks left in the year and there have been more than 200,000 job losses across the tech industry. Here are the details.
articles.body:
We've been inundated with tech layoffs throughout the whole of 2026 — and there's likely more to come in the final few weeks of the year. In June, 14,000 job cuts happened at EV automaker Lucid, game developer Bungie, trading platform company Robinhood and others. Microsoft 's round of layoffs in July affected 4,800 jobs — mostly across its Xbox gaming division. Following that, companies like Samsung, Zillow and even TikTok joined the club.

According to many reports , the U.S. is at the center of these job cuts. Oracle has had the biggest impact on layoffs this year so far. The annual financial disclosure the company filed on June 23 showed the software giant cut 21,000 jobs over the past year, roughly 13% of its workforce.

"The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce," Oracle said in the filing.

In response to the numerous job cuts, California Governor Gavin Newsom in June unveiled a tool to track AI's impact on the workforce . "As AI advances, we aren't just watching from the sidelines; we're reimagining how we prepare California through strong governance and innovative policy." In addition, more than 4,500 Google workers signed a petition calling for layoff protections as things get worse. Some of the protections they're asking for include buyouts before mandatory layoffs and guaranteed severance.

TrueUp finds that layoffs seem to be moving at a faster rate than last year — over 245,000 workers in tech were let go in 2025, while there have been more than 200,000 layoffs in 2026 so far. Several of the companies below have laid off employees due to increased spending in AI. We'll get into the reasons for the layoffs.

Disney is reportedly planning to lay off thousands in an effort to cut annual costs by 20%. Layoffs have not been confirmed yet, but we'll update this story if and when they are. According to people familiar with the matter, the cost reductions could come from layoffs in addition to expense reductions.

Intel reportedly initiated another round of layoffs this month, primarily affecting its IT organization. The number of jobs affected this time hasn't been disclosed. This is just the latest in a number of layoffs at Intel in 2026 that, in total, have affected hundreds of employees.

Ubisoft's latest round of layoffs has reportedly affected 166 jobs, mostly in its Montreal and Quebec hubs. Ubisoft representatives told IGN that the job cuts were accounting for an "evolving portfolio and changing production needs."

Polymarket staff reportedly experienced layoffs, but the scope of which is not known. The reports also suggest the company has reduced the number of contractors it will work with moving forward, particularly in the marketing department.

Squarespace, the website-building company, is laying off 19% of its workforce, which amounts to about 300 people. "The changes are intended to simplify how we operate, sharpen our priorities and enable the company to move faster as we position Squarespace for its next phase of growth," Jeff Seedman, a representative from Squarespace, told TechCrunch. Squarespace's industry has been disrupted by AI, as "vibe-coding" website builders have become more popular.

Design software company Canva's recent layoffs will impact 22% of its staff, or just over 1,200 employees. According to reports , the company is reorganizing its business and merging its product, growth and platform teams. Canva is also looking to reduce "subspecialisation," which could result in remaining employees taking on more responsibilities.

Fintech company Block started its second round of layoffs recently, after cutting more than 4,000 jobs earlier this year. According to reports , the Jack Dorsey-led company hasn't disclosed how many jobs were affected this time around, but reportedly teams at Cash App and Square (both owned by Block) were affected.

Amazon reportedly laid off "fewer than 1,000 white-collar workers" in its stores division. That's the part of the company that oversees the tech giant's e-commerce website. Employees in the U.S., India and the United Kingdom were reportedly affected.

In an additional incident, Amazon laid off about 250 employees in its devices and services unit, according to a Reuters report . This comes after a number of new product announcements, including new Kindles and Echo devices . According to the report, the cuts mostly affect those in software development.

The cloud storage company Dropbox is laying off about 9% of its workforce, which accounts for roughly 200 employees. The job cuts primarily affect workers on the engineering, product, design, and G&A teams. "Today, we're making difficult choices about where we invest and how we organize Dropbox to achieve the product and growth priorities that will matter most for our long-term strategy," Dropbox co-CEO Ashraf Alkarmi said in an email to staff. Alkarmi also announced that, alongside the layoffs, chief technology officer Ali Dasdan will step down.

While not officially new layoffs just yet, reports claim Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees. This is in an effort to further reduce costs in the wake of increased AI usage. According to the reports, Xbox, Windows, Copilot and finance divisions will be participating in the offer. Microsoft already laid off thousands of workers so far in 2026.

EBay will reportedly cut 9% of its workforce in an effort to streamline operations. The latest job cuts come after a previous round of layoffs back in February, which affected about 800 positions. "As we work to capture the significant opportunity ahead, this step was taken to ensure we continue to operate from a position of strength by aligning our teams and resources with our top strategic priorities," an eBay spokesperson said in a statement.

Vide game publisher EA will eliminate 400 jobs , or about 3% of its workforce. This includes shutting down BioWare , the development studio behind the Mass Effect games. The next Mass Effect title will be cancelled as a result of the layoffs. These job cuts come after EA told investors earlier this year that it would reduce research and development costs as part of a plan to save upwards of $700 million.

According to a report in The Wall Street Journal, Netflix will lay off about 1,000 people, which accounts for about 6% of its global workforce. The report says the bulk of the layoffs will affect Netflix's "product, tech, legal and human-resources teams." This latest round of layoffs is the biggest for the company since 2022, and it comes in the wake of Netflix struggling to increase customer engagement and overall growth.

A "large part" of the Airtable team was laid off on October 12. Federico Simionato, Airtable owner Bending Spoons' product leader, said on X that the layoffs were not due to the workers' abilities but rather the company's "deep belief that small teams ship more and better." The exact number of employees affected by the layoffs wasn't disclosed.

Workday will be laying off around 140 employees from the Bay Area, as part of an effort to trim its tech team. The cuts come as part of a broader plan to cut the company's global workforce by 2.5%.

Xbox announced it eliminated 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios and additional areas of the Xbox Game Studios division. These layoffs are part of a "reset" it announced this summer; the company already laid off 1,600 people in July, and said at the time that an additional 1,600 terminations were still to come.

According to a Bloomberg report , Apple has laid off an undisclosed number of employees from Fitness+, the company's exercise subscription service. According to the report, the layoffs affected those who worked in the audio side of the division, which includes features like Time to Walk and Time to Run guided audio workouts. Reportedly, offerings like this will be reduced — but not eliminated completely — from the service.

Oracle employees were impacted by yet another round of layoffs in September. The total number of employees laid off this time around is not currently known. The tech giant reportedly set employees early morning emails on Monday, September 14, letting those affected know it would be their last working day. It's also reported that, with these layoffs, Oracle is looking to offset the amount of money is pouring into AI chips and data centers. Earlier this year, Oracle laid off 21,000 people.

Uber announced it will cut 3,300 jobs, or about 10% of its workforce, in a big restructuring effort. "We are removing layers, simplifying team structures, refining our global location strategy, and focusing our people and investments against the biggest opportunities ahead of us," CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in a statement . While the cuts apply to both regular employees and managers, the company stated it will reduce the "number of employees who sit 7+ layers from the CEO" by 20%, and it will cut the number of "micro-teams" by almost 50%. The CEO's memo did not mention AI as catalyst for the layoffs, but it did explain that this restructuring will allow Uber to bring its services to more people, invest in more drivers and merchants and "build the autonomous future."

According to an AppleInsider report , Apple laid off at least 60 people in its Vision Group, which is the team responsible for the Vision Pro VR headset. A Bloomberg report notes that Apple is also laying off roles in its Intelligent Systems Experience group, which is partially responsible for some of the AI systems on Apple devices. Overall, its estimated the layoffs affect more than 200 people.

When it comes to Vision Group and Vision Pro, it's been reported that incoming CEO John Ternus would be putting that product category "on ice," so this seems like the start of that process. The Vision Pro headset came out in 2024 with an eye-watering $3,699 starting price, and it remains to be seen if Apple will be pulling out of the AR/VR category entirely in the future. The Intelligence Systems changes are reportedly tied to changes that are necessary for the technical architecture for Apple's newly AI-infused Siri.

The New York Times reported that TikTok will lay off 250 people and close its Nashville, Tennessee office in October. This location was home to, in part, some of TikTok's content moderation team, although the company has not specified the reason for the layoffs or which teams they primarily affect. "We have decided to close our Nashville office to streamline our operations and better align our teams for long-term growth," a press officer for what is known as the TikTok U.S.D.S. Joint Venture said in a statement to the Times.

Zillow will lay off just over 500 people as it enacts organizational changes across the company. "These are difficult decisions that reflect both the strides we're making in our strategy and the reality of what is required of us to grow at scale," CEO Jeremy Wacksman wrote in a press release . Wacksman didn't go into detail about what organizational changes were made, or which departments are bearing the brunt of the layoffs. "These changes are about ensuring we have a disciplined cost structure and getting more efficient, with the right people in the right positions," he wrote.

Etsy laid off about 220 people, or 12% of its workforce, as it attempts to simplify its organizational structure. The cuts primarily affected the product and engineering teams, and Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal said that the layoffs were necessary to build "the organization we believe Etsy needs for the future." An Etsy spokesperson told CNBC that the cuts were not driven by artificial intelligence adoption.

Microsoft has begun another round of layoffs that affects 4,800 jobs , or around 2.1% of its workforce. The Xbox division is getting hit the hardest, with 3,200 roles getting cut through fiscal year 2027, Xbox chief Asha Sharma said in a post on X — 1,600 people were let go on July 6. Shortly after those layoffs were revealed, it was announced that Sharma was appointed to a U.S. Federal Reserve task force to help advise it on "productivity and jobs." Other appointees include Marc Andreessen of Andreessen Horowitz and Charles I. Jones, professor of economics at Stanford University.

Intel is reportedly downsizing its data center group, despite strong performance. The company hasn't disclosed how many roles would be affected.

Visa will be cutting about 2,600 jobs, which amounts to about 7% of its workforce. The layoffs will primarily affect the technology and product teams, and the impetus in part is to make the company more efficient. "To capture the opportunities ahead and best position Visa to lead this transformation, we must continue evolving how we work," Chief Executive Officer Ryan McInerney wrote in a memo. "AI is also helping to accelerate this evolution and shape the way work gets done at Visa." But according to Bloomberg's report, AI was not the only factor to influence Visa's decision to do these layoffs. The company reportedly intends to reinvest in things like consumer payments and value-added services like stablecoin.

Software company Monday.com will be laying off 20% of its workforce, which comes out to about 630 people. This comes as the company makes a pivot to AI and is attempting to make its AI platform a core offering of its business. Earlier this year, it designed its main product around the idea that business customers increasingly want its employees to work with AI agents.

Patreon laid off 20% of its workforce, or 93 people, as a result of the company "changing our organizational structure and how we work." But Patreon was explicit in its email to creators and staff that "we are not making the above changes because we believe AI replaces humans." However, the email also said "AI has fundamentally transformed the tech industry, though, including how we work."

Uber has reportedly laid off 10% of its customer service division, according to a Bloomberg report, as it looks to "embrace artificial intelligence" and simplify its ranks. The company also stated in May that it would slow hiring as it makes use of AI more internally.

Samsung is eliminating 179 jobs as it moves its New Jersey headquarters to Texas later this year. The move is expected to impact around 1,000 workers. We're now getting a fuller picture of what that looks like: according to Reuters , 739 roles at Samsung's New Jersey location have been affected in some way. Some have been offered relocation packages as the company shifts its headquarters to Texas, while others have been let go. In addition, it's reported that 100 roles in its Texas location, primarily in the mobile division, have also been let go.

Amazon will lay off some people in its artificial general intelligence group, although the company has not disclosed how many roles will be affected. "This is a fast-moving space, and we're sharpening our focus on the initiatives that matter most for customers, so we can move faster on what counts," an Amazon spokesperson told CNBC.

Sony Interactive Entertainment released a statement that it's cutting "a significant number of employees" from its Bungie workforce. That includes most of the Destiny team and some Marathon team members, as well as SIE teams that support Bungie's operations. The email didn't say how many employees were affected.

Electric vehicle maker Lucid announced it's cutting around 18% of its workforce, and also noted COO Marc Winterhoff's leaving the company, Reuters reported . The layoffs are in an effort to "​boost profitability amid growing competition." The cuts affect full-time employees, contractors and hourly manufacturing workers.

Cloud computing services company Rackspace laid off 750 workers , or around 15% of its workforce. The cuts are driven by a shift in focus toward AI.

EV company Rivian let go of hundreds of employees , which amounts to around 2% of the company's workforce, the Wall Street Journal reported . Those affected were part of Rivian's service and customer organization, which handled marketing and sales.

Trading platform company Robinhood is planning to lay off 10% of its staff to restructure, the Robinhood Comms account shared on X today — that's around 290 jobs. It's unclear if the layoffs are AI-related, but CEO Vlad Tenev noted the company will be "utilizing frontier technologies to push our execution even further."

Salesforce laid off at least 86 employees in California, though Business Insider sources say job cuts also occurred in Washington and outside the U.S. as well. The cuts reportedly affect employees involved with Salesforce's Agentforce AI product, Mulesoft IT integration tool and its Marketing Cloud software.

Groupon is planning to lay off roughly 25% of its workforce , which will result in 400 job cuts. Those positions are expected to be eliminated by the end of the third quarter. This is in an effort to restructure the company and rebuild it as an AI-native company.

In another set of AI-related layoffs, website builder Wix said it was cutting around 20% of staff. Wix cofounder and CEO Avishai Abrahami announced the cuts on X , pointing to the changes AI is bringing to the industry and stating "we need to become a faster, leaner, and flatter organization." He also put part of the blame on the Israeli Shekel to U.S. Dollar exchange rates, which impact the company because it's based in Israel. The cuts are expected to impact around 1,000 roles, based on Wix's headcount.

Webflow, a website builder and hosting company, conducted a round of layoffs that an employee called "a bloodbath" in a statement to the San Francisco Chronicle . It's unclear how many employees were impacted, but one anonymous developer from the company told the Chronicle they believe it was larger than Webflow's last major round of layoffs, which affected 8% of its workforce in 2024. As with other recent layoffs, it looks like a shift to AI is to blame here. "AI is rewriting the rules for how marketing teams create, test, and optimize digital experiences," CEO Linda Tong said in a statement . "And the companies that move decisively through moments like this are the ones that come out ahead."

ClickUp CEO Zeb Evans announced that the company cut 22% of its workforce as it turns toward AI to improve productivity. He claimed it "wasn't about cutting costs," but about funneling savings from the cuts "directly back into the people who stay." The company has introduced million-dollar salary bands reserved for employees who "create outsized impact using AI."

Intuit is planning to lay off 3,000 employees, or about 17% of its workforce, Reuters reports . CEO Sasan Goodarzi sent a memo to employees noting the layoffs would help the company's efforts of focusing on infusing AI across its services.

Meta has officially begun cutting 10% of its workforce , totaling around 8,000 employees. In addition, it plans to close 6,000 open roles. The reason is to allow more room for AI spending.

Like Microsoft, NPR is offering voluntary buyouts to 300 employees in the newsroom, but only 30 will be accepted. However, if the news organization doesn't receive its target number, it will result in targeted layoffs. The reason is due to the loss of federal funding.

The online retail giant cut more jobs this month, this time from the Selling Partner Services organization. These new layoffs come after Amazon cut roughly 30,000 jobs in rounds across October and January. A spokesperson told Business Insider that the most recent layoffs have affected a "small number" of employees. The Selling Partner Services team works with third-party merchants on Amazon, providing onboarding, logistics and account management support.

Cisco is cutting just under 4,000 jobs in Q4, CEO Chuck Robbins said in a blog post . Impacted employees will receive pro-rated payment of 2026 bonuses and will also receive "support in finding new opportunities" via Cisco's placement services. In June, it was confirmed that the layoffs include 471 workers in the Bay Area .

"While we are reducing roles in some areas, we are making clear, strategic investments — particularly in silicon, optics, security, and in our employees' use of AI across the company," Robbins said.

LinkedIn is planning to lay off 5% of its staff, which is around 875 employees, Reuters reports . An anonymous person told Reuters the reason is to reorganize teams and focus employees on areas ⁠where its business is growing. However, one of the sources said the reason was "not for artificial intelligence to replace jobs at LinkedIn."

GM is letting go of around 500 to 600 employees in the Information Technology sector, Bloomberg reports . The reason is to "trim costs and clear the way to bring in staff with skills in other technology areas."

Due to restructuring driven by AI, Cloudflare is cutting more than 1,100 employees . "Today's actions are not a cost-cutting exercise or an assessment of individuals' performance; They are about Cloudflare defining how a world-class, high-growth company operates and creates value in the agentic AI era," Prince and President Michelle Zatlyn said in an email to employees .

PayPal is planning to cut around 20% of its staff — nearly 4,800 employees — over the next few years, according to the Wall Street Journal . "First, we will remove duplication and layers from our organizational structure. Second, we will accelerate our AI adoption and automation across our operations," CEO Enrique Lores said to investors.

Cryptocurrency platform Coinbase is laying off 700 employees , which amounts to around 14% of its staff. CEO Brian Armstrong cites the current market and AI changing the way they work as reasons for the layoffs.

Microsoft is offering a first-ever buyout to up to 7% of its employees, CNBC reports . It's a one-time retirement program that's available for workers at the senior director level and below whose years of employment and age are 70 or higher.

Nike announced it's laying off 1,400 people this week. "Collectively, these changes will result in a reduction of approximately 1,400 roles in global operations, with the majority in technology," COO Venkatesh Alagirisamy said. "These reductions are very hard for the teammates directly affected and for the teams around them, too."

Amazon is planning to temporarily close a warehouse in Homestead, Florida, which will eliminate more than 600 jobs, Newsweek reports . The job cuts will start in July and continue through September but the giant company is giving employees the option to relocate to other facilities. The warehouse has only been open for just under two years but Amazon is already looking to update the site.

Battery recycling company Redwood Materials laid off 10% of its employees, totaling 135 people, TechCrunch reports . Those who were let go received an email from the chief HR officer telling them the layoffs were made "to sharpen our focus, our work and the size of our teams to support the direction Redwood is going in the future."

Snap is laying off 1,000 workers , which is 16% of its staff, Variety reports . The Snapchat parent company made the announcement just weeks after Irenic Capital Management asked the company to make changes to improve performance and revenue.

Snap is using AI to streamline operations and assist the now smaller workforce. "We have already witnessed small squads leveraging AI tools to drive meaningful progress across several important initiatives," Snap CEO Evan Spiegel said.

Just two months after taking over as CEO of Disney, Josh D'Amaro announced the company is laying off 1,000 of its employees, AP News reports . In addition, Marvel let 8% of its staff go after the call was made.

"Over the past several months, we have looked at ways in which we can streamline our operations in various parts of the company to ensure we deliver the world-class creativity and innovation our fans value and expect from Disney," D'Amaro said in a memo to employees. "Given the fast-moving pace of our industries, this requires us to constantly assess how to foster a more agile and technologically-enabled workforce to meet tomorrow's needs."

The wearable camera maker this year will eliminate 145 employees due to a restructuring plan to cut costs, the Wall Street Journal reported . The cuts are expected to last until the end of the year.

Vimeo is going through its third round of layoffs since it was acquired by Bending Spoons. This time, the company let go of more than 120 people, which is about 25% of its city staff .

It's been reported that 200 Meta employees in the Bay Area will lose their jobs at the end of May. That includes 124 employees in Burlingame and 74 in Sunnyvale. The company last laid off workers just a few weeks ago.

Oracle has begun implementing a big cull of its employee base . On the final day of March, more than a dozen Oracle employees announced on LinkedIn they had been let go from their jobs, Business Insider reports . It's unclear at this time how many workers were affected, but it was projected to be thousands at the start of this month.

Those laid off received the same email : "After careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role as part of a broader organizational change."

The job cuts are reportedly to help Oracle stem a cash drain related its expenditures on AI infrastructure. In June, Oracle revealed that it had laid off 21,000 people as part of the cuts.

Deux Ex studio Eidos-Montréal announced on March 30 that it's laying off 124 people . In response, the studio head David Anfossi has decided to leave the company.

The cuts are a result of "changing project needs and impacts across production and support teams," the gaming company said in a LinkedIn post . It also noted that the decision to lay off these employees is not related to their talent or performance.

After already having layoffs in January , T-Mobile has cut even more of its workers, GeekWire reports . It's unclear how many people were laid off at this time, but it could be in the hundreds.

"To move even faster in a dynamic market while continuing to deliver best-in-class digital experiences for our customers, we're further aligning our IT organization to support future growth and innovation… This includes the difficult decision of eliminating some roles while continuing to invest and hire in areas," T-Mobile told GeekWire in a statement.

Meta began laying off hundreds of employees on March 25, totaling around 700 people, per The New York Times . Those impacted were part of the Reality Labs team, as well as social media and recruiting teams. Though still significant, this is a much smaller number compared to a Reuters report that suggested 20% off staff would be affected by layoffs due to the increased spending on AI.

This change comes as the company is shifting away from its metaverse creation, which includes Horizon Worlds for its Quest VR headset that's operated by the Reality Labs team.

The gaming giant on March 24 announced it was laying off more than 1,000 workers in an effort to right-size the staff of its popular free-to-play online shooter, Fortnite. CEO Tim Sweeney sent a note to his staff, citing the reason for the layoffs is due to the "downturn in Fortnite engagement," which means "we're spending significantly more than we're making, and we have to make major cuts to keep the company funded." He made it a point to note the layoffs are not related to AI.

105 employees from the Red Storm Entertainment team were laid off by Ubisoft in an effort to cut costs, IGN reports . Game development has ended at the studio, so the downsizing will remain permanent. The company employed 180 people in 2022 but has seen multiple layoffs over the years.

Roughly 1,600 employees were laid off at Atlassian on March 16, which is around 10% of total workers. Ahead of the layoffs, Atlassian CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes shared a message with the entire team, letting them know the reason is to "self-fund further investment in AI and enterprise sales, while strengthening our financial profile. We're also changing the way we work and reorganising around our System of Work to move faster." Impacted employees received an email shortly after this message went out.

articles.title: PlayStation's Black Friday Sale Is Almost Over - Here Are The Best Deals You Can Still Get
articles.summary: PlayStation’s Black Friday 2026 sale includes deep discounts on PS5 games like Ghost of Yotei, Marvel's Wolverine, and Death Stranding 2, plus $20 off DualSense controllers and $100 off refurbished PS5 consoles.
articles.body:
PlayStation's Black Friday deals are now live , and there's a lot more to look forward to than just digital releases.

While Sony's earlier Black Friday promotion was limited to digital deals , we're now seeing price drops on peripherals, physical games, and accessories.

Yes, yes, most of us will be fully occupied playing Grand Theft Auto 6 for the rest of the year, but if you're after some rad bargains on other great games from this year, or fancy picking up an extra controller without paying full price, there's plenty worth checking out right now.

PlayStation 5 - Digital Edition 1TB - Certified Refurbished

PlayStation 5 - 1TB - Certified Refurbished

PlayStation 5 - 825GB - Certified Refurbished

We were hoping the ongoing RAM crisis wouldn't make any big problems for PS5 buyers this year, but it's just not the case, sadly. There are no confirmed PS5 console deals for Black Friday 2026 at the time of writing, even with PlayStation's sale expanding to physical media and hardware.

This year, however, there's no change to the MSRP outside of saving around $100 on a refurbished console. You can find a PS5 slim digital edition for $499 , $100 off its MSRP for the standard console. Refurbished disc edition consoles, again the slim variant, are $549, also $100 in savings .

If you're after a PS5 Pro, my advice is to also keep an eye on PlayStation's online store . The gaming giant has been occasionally restocking the sought after console (which adds a few nifty ray tracing upgrades to GTA 6, albeit not 60 frames per second) for $899. Which, while still expensive, is nothing compared to what these bad boys are going for on the resale market right now (upwards of $1500).

Metal Gear Solid: The Master Collection Vol. 2

PS5 gamers have a ton of choice for new games to play, including big discounts on games from this year and other recent releases.

Walmart has great games like the Resident Evil 4 Remake and Borderlands 4 for $15, and at $30 you can grab 2026 hits like Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, Resident Evil Requiem and Saros, as well as The Blood of Dawnwalker.

Assassin’s Creed Shadows - Limited Edition (Amazon Exclusive)

Street Fighter 6 Years 1-2 Fighters Edition

Outside of this $15/$30 sale at Walmart, Ghost of Yotei has jumped out as a top Black Friday PS5 deal so far in general. It's a wonderful experience, and one of my favorite games I've played this year (as I thankfully managed to get round to it). It's currently down to just $34.99, 50% off its MSRP. That's what I like to call a proper Black Friday deal, where you're getting a truly significant discount that's an easy buy.

If you want to bundle the story expansion DLC in, you can do so by opting for the Complete Edition instead, which is down to $49.99 at Amazon and also includes the Legends multiplayer content.

If you're looking for some spandex-clad ultraviolence, then look no further than Insomniac's latest Marvel romp, Wolverine . It's perhaps not on the level of the developer's Spider-Man games, but at $20 off, now could be the time to try it if you haven't already.

As for other titles, Death Stranding 2 is now just $37.99, while you can pick up Spider-Man 2, Stellar Blade, and God of War Ragnarok for under $30.

Up to $30 Off DualSense Controllers for Black Friday

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Gray Camouflage

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Cosmic Red

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller - White

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Starlight Blue

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Galactic Purple

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Midnight Black

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller - Sterling Silver

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Chroma Teal

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Chroma Indigo

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Chroma Pearl

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – 007 First Light Limited Edition

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Marathon Limited Edition

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Remix Green

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Rhythm Blue

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Techno Red

That includes the DualSense controllers, which have received their regularly scheduled yearly discount down to $54. There's a few different varieties available, at a few different prices, but most are discounted and available at the cheapest you'll typically find them all year round.

Sony has marked down every available DualSense color by $20 this year - including limited edition controllers that hardly ever see any discounts. After Sony quietly increased the price of all DualSense controllers , this sale should help ease that sting a bit.

The cheapest options are going to be the standard white, Midnight Black, Gray Camo, and the Galaxy Collection (Cosmic Red, Starlight Blue, and Galactic Purple) colors for $54, while the newer colors, including the Chroma Collection , are $60.

For those looking for a more premium gaming experience, consider picking up the DualSense Edge. Currently, the white controller is $30 off and Midnight Black is also $30 off as part of this year's sale.

PlayStation 5 DualSense Wireless Controller - White

If you’re looking for the lowest price on a PlayStation 5 DualSense Controller, Woot has the best deal going on a “Grade A Refurbished” model with a 90-day Limited Warranty for added peace of mind. It’s down to $39.99 on the Amazon-owned website, and Prime members even get free shipping. That’s nearly 50% off the list price, but only the white colorway is discounted.

The DualSense has remained IGN’s top PS5 controller for a reason. I mean, it does come in the box with the console. From the familiar, comfortable design to the features that help enhance gameplay, there’s a lot to love, and it’s especially great for cruising the streets of Vice City in GTA VI .

Black Friday deals are more confusing than ever these days. Most retailers spend November teasing limited-time offers, but the reality is that the deepest discounts typically arrive a lot earlier than you'd expect.

Having tracked gaming sales for years, one thing is clear: once a deal hits from an official gaming sale like this one, it usually sticks for the rest of the month at least.

That means the prices you see now on games and accessories are very likely the ones that’ll hold through to December. If you’ve been holding out for a solid deal, there’s no need to wait any longer.

These offers are reliable, worthwhile, and unlikely to get any better. In fact, some deals are so good, they could even sell out before you get the chance to buy them if you decide to wait around anymore. My advice? Grab the games and hardware you’ve had your eye on, there’s no risk of Black Friday regret. Trust me on this!

Want more gaming deals? I've left the rest of the best PS5 deals in the Black Friday sale just below, but you should also keep an eye out for the rest of our coverage over the next few weeks. And, heads up, Nintendo is also kicking off their official Black Friday sale soon on November 22 , so there's a whole lot more to look forward to.

Marvel's Wolverine - Digital Deluxe Edition

Control Resonant - Digital Deluxe Edition

The Blood of Dawnwalker - Eclipse Edition

Why You Should Still Buy Physical PS5 Games

I'll admit I'm a little biased here, but I really do think there's still plenty of life left in physical games - even if Sony doesn't.

Sony is planning to stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation releases from January 2028, meaning disc-based games are on the chopping block. While existing physical releases won't suddenly disappear, the prospect of future PlayStation games becoming digital-only is a worrying one for anyone who enjoys building a collection or wants to be able to play their games when the servers inevitably shut down one day.

Sony has attributed the decision to changing consumer preferences, so if we want physical games to stick around, we need to make our voices heard where it matters most: our wallets.

Buying physical gives you options that digital downloads simply don't. You can lend games to friends, trade them in, sell them when you're finished, or keep building a collection that you can actually see and hold. Physical retailers also compete with one another on pricing, meaning you're not entirely at the mercy of the PlayStation Store when hunting for a bargain.

There's a wider ecosystem worth supporting, too, from independent game shops and second-hand retailers to collectors and gaming preservationists. An increasingly digital-only future means fewer choices over where we buy our games, how much we pay, and what we can do with them afterwards.

So, if you've been sitting on the fence about picking up a physical copy of a game you've been eyeing, perhaps now's the time. Keep building that collection, support the retailers still selling physical games, and show Sony there's still an audience for discs. Buying a few games won't single-handedly reverse its decision, but if we stop buying them altogether, we're hardly going to convince anyone to keep making them.

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides .

articles.title: This gaming mouse should be a Logitech-killer, but it has one big flaw
articles.summary: Keychron G6 HE gaming mouse hands-on impressions: Hall effect magnetic switches like Logitech’s G Pro Superstrike mice aren’t quite the same without haptics.
articles.body: When Keychron announced its $90 G6 HE gaming mouse, I immediately thought, “Cool! A cheaper alternative to the pricey $180 Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike.” Logitech’s innovation with the Superstrike is using magnetic Hall effect switches for a user-adjustable mouse click depth, with haptic vibrations mimicking the tactile click feel. The Keychron G6 HE, as its name indicates, also uses Hall effect switches for that same kind of customization. But something felt immediately off as I began testing it. The mouse’s shape and design are very reminiscent of Logitech G Pro models, with more colorful flair. The magnetic switches are there and easily customizable (through a browser-based app, no less). But the clicks? The clicks are all wrong. The left and right mouse buttons on the G6 HE use Keychron’s MagOptic switches, which are both magnetic Hall effect and optical. They click just like any standard mouse, regardless of where you set the actuation point. There are no fancy haptics on the Keychron. If you set the buttons to a shallow hair-trigger depth, you’ll register a press before you actually feel or hear any click. Set the depth for a very heavy press, and the mouse clicks before it actually registers. That… kind of defeats the purpose here. [Product: Keychron G6 HE UltraLight wireless mouse | There’s not much point in tuning the actuation depth of the G6 HE’s buttons if the click feel doesn’t match it. I suppose it’s still nice to have a hair-trigger-like setting for taking faster single shots in an FPS, but not feeling anything when you shoot is weird. And it gets frustrating when using the G6 HE as a regular mouse for productivity — like you’re getting phantom clicks as you mouse around your computer. At least I can feel my accidental clicks when using a Logitech Superstrike with the action set too high, and I know I’m to blame for leaving the mouse on my try-hard settings. I reached out to Keychron for the reasoning behind the G6 HE’s magnetic-but-not-haptic setup, and cofounder Fab Chan said, “There are two reasons for this design. First, many users still prefer the feel of a traditional click over haptics. Second, a haptic motor adds weight, and for this model we prioritized a lighter design. That said, we’re planning a model with haptic feedback. It will be slightly heavier than the G6 HE, and we’ll share more details soon.” [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The G6 HE is a lightweight mouse. It’s only 49g with its battery, or 40g in wired mode with the battery removed. The Logitech X2 Superstrike is 60g, and the newer X3 Superstrike is 59g — each still pretty light. If you ignore all the Hall effect stuff and just use the G6 HE as a regular mouse, it has some things going for it over the Superstrikes. In addition to its lighter build and much lower price, it feels a tiny bit comfier in my hand, thanks to its side walls that curve slightly inward at the bottom. One of its best features is hot-swappable batteries. From my time testing Angry Miao’s AM Infinity Mouse, I know that once you can pop out a magnetic battery pack and quickly swap it, you never want to go back to plugging in your mouse to charge. You can also get the G6 HE in black with a standard built-in rechargeable battery for $15 less, but I don’t think that’s enough savings to forgo the convenience of hot-swap batteries. The G6 HE’s charging base doubles as the wireless receiver, and of course it’s lit up with customizable RGB lighting. It has four programmable buttons for on-the-fly changes to things like DPI, lighting, mouse profiles, or just about anything else you want to program. The browser-based Keychron Launcher software is robust and makes tinkering with the G6 HE or its base very easy. And for some reason, the receiver / charging base is designed like a vacuum tube, which is fun, but it means you’re unscrewing its clear housing to access the battery — a little tedious. [Image: Keychron’s Launcher web app is very simple to use. It works much like VIA for keyboards, but it’s tailored to Keychron boards and mice. I can’t shake my disappointment with the G6 HE’s lackadaisical magnetic switch implementation. Keychron seems proud of the fancy MagOptic Switch it put into the G6 HE, even going so far as to call it “next gen,” but this mouse seems a jack of all trades and master of none. The G6 HE is cheaper than most other mice with hot-swap batteries — which can still make it worthwhile if you don’t care about all the Hall effect stuff — but that is its lone saving grace. We’ll have to wait and see if Keychron’s follow-up model with haptics can properly compete with the Superstrike mice and their hallmark feature. I’m excited to see where Hall effect tech goes in mice, and how more companies can evolve it, but the G6 HE is a half-measure. Photography by Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge

articles.title: Yaga Finale Review Gives Us A Shocking Reveal, Executed to Perfection With a Stunning Cast
articles.summary: Episodes 7 and 8 of Yaga reveal the incredible and shocking twist we've all been waiting for, executed to perfection with a stunning cast and phenomenal writing.
articles.body:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Yaga Season 1, episodes 7 and 8. The full season is now streaming on AMC+ in the US and Crave in Canada.

The first part of the two-episode finale of Yaga opens with the Baba Yaga narrator saying, “it always has to be three…” as we see Rapp wandering in the woods at the ritual space. He looks down, puzzled, to see a red cooler on the ground with fish inside, and within that a ceramic jar made by Olena (Laney, as we know her) – and the jar has testicles in it. He blinks, and is still holding the jar and has the cooler, but is standing out on the dock near Carson’s boat at the marina.

We see Henry’s parents for the first time at the coroners, where they are looking at Henry’s body. We find out Henry was brutally murdered one week ago, with chicken feathers shoved down his throat before being burned alive. The pathologist, Jake, confirms he was castrated prior to death, as well.

As Rapp tells Henry’s mother, Dora, that he disagrees with Geena having been the one to murder him – he shares his own clues we’ve seen him gather over the past few episodes regarding Baba Yaga – and it’s clear that everyone in the room thinks he’s crazy. Dora tells him sternly that he had one job to do, and that was to protect Henry – and she fires him on the spot. As she walks away, Rapp tells her, “I know where all your bodies are buried.” Yet, Dora does not seem concerned about the threat.

Carson confronts Eckert about Geena previously sharing how he threatened and physically assaulted her – he only denies it, all while trying to make Carson feel guilty for even thinking something so awful of him. A lovely icing on the cake for someone who seems to be trying to cover their tracks while using manipulation tactics.

We see that Rapp has snuck up into Olena’s room at the hospital to try and pull more information out of her regarding Baba Yaga, as he believes, based on his discoveries, there will be a third murder following Logan and Henry’s. As usual, Olena is being evasive and cheeky, until Rapp pulls out her journal. For the first time, we see her looking legitimately concerned about this being in his hands, as he begins speaking the words written down in Ukrainian.

Olena starts to work with him on this for reasons unknown, and Rapp guesses that not only are there three murders planned, but there are three Yagas. Olena responds with, “Three to live forever,” as Rapp starts to put the puzzle pieces together – the third and youngest Yaga needs to have a baby to continue the cycle.

Right when we think Olena might actually reveal who the youngest Yaga is, she tells Rapp a sacrifice is needed before she divulges that the sacrifice is a kiss for her. All that’s needed is one kiss, but Rapp ends up becoming entranced and begins making out with Olena as he sees flashes of her as a young woman on the bed, surrounded by flowers. She ends up saying the third Yaga is “onuka,” which translates to “granddaughter” – confirming she herself must be the oldest Yaga, but it’s unclear who her granddaughter is. She takes off her top and right as he’s going further with her, Katherine barges into the room and yells, “What are you doing to my mother?!”

Rapp, shocked that Katherine is Olena’s daughter and convinced she is connected to the murders, begs Carson to go with him to Katherine’s house to try and get any other morsel of intel. As they’re sitting at Katherine’s dining table, discussing this (calmly at first), Rapp drops his conclusion, saying, “I think you, your mother, and your daughter are a multigenerational team of serial killers who think they are witches, who are punishing bad men for hurting women.”

Katherine looks unimpressed, saying, “Well that sounds fucking fantastic.” As this is all happening, Carson looks to be slightly restless, fidgeting every so often while Rapp and Katherine argue through this all. After voices raise, arguments escalate, and Rapp accuses Katherine of murdering Henry and lying about it, Katherine kicks them out of her house. While they are leaving, she also puts Rapp in his place, reminding him that every time he came on to her, he had an ulterior motive. She says to him, “I don’t buy your act. I am ancient, you stupid little boy,” and the line is delivered brilliantly.

Rapp is continuing to try and convince Carson he is correct with his theory, and explaining the pattern of “333” that he’s seen basically everywhere during his time in Whittock. He believes the third victim will be killed the following morning on March 3rd at 3:33am. Before Carson heads to meet with Dora, who has requested a private meeting with her at an upscale bar, she begs Rapp to wait in his hotel room for her until she figures out the next steps they should take. He eventually gives in, and she kisses him goodbye, hoping he will trust her on this.

Immediately, the meeting with Dora seems to have an underlying tone of danger to Carson, as Dora blames Henry’s horrific behavior on his father, saying he came after both her and Alice (Logan’s mother) when they were young – it is unclear if it was consensual or not. We get confirmation that Henry and Logan were in fact half brothers, which is more disturbing after knowing they previously had some type of infatuation with one another… and acted on it.

It’s starts to be pretty clear that Dora’s ulterior motive was wanting to keep the fact that Henry raped Lily under wraps. In turn, she offers a job to Carson “for life” working for the Parks. Carson politely declines, and Dora comments, “If you’re working for Eckert, you’re already working for us.” As this information sinks in, Dora unsurprisingly leaves her with a threat before walking away.

Rapp, continuing his hunt to find out who the third Yaga and killer is, sweet-talks his way into Pam’s apartment by means of her roommate. While there, he discovers the witch mask, along with Henry’s watch – and shockingly, that Pam is on a date with Eckert, making him potentially the next victim.

As we get to the end of the episode, Rapp calls Carson to fill her in on his findings, saying he’s heading to the woods and thinks he knows how to make Baba Yaga’s cabin magically appear. He tells her he needs her to meet him there – that he needs a partner. As she hesitantly agrees, she picks up Eckert as well, and we find out (disturbingly) that Eckert was in fact supposed to be on a date with Pam, but she stood him up. Along with that, Olena is missing from the hospital, and Katherine is not picking up her phone.

Episode 8 picks up right where Episode 7 ended, with Rapp in the woods searching for Baba Yaga’s cabin.

After prying, Eckert admits to Carson the truth of what he did to Geena and that he covered up Lily’s sexual assault – saying he did it for his kid. But Carson shows no sympathy. At this point, Rapp is already deep in the forest, speaking spells in Ukrainian and following a line of chickens to find Baba Yaga’s cabin. All of a sudden, he stumbles upon it, seeing warm lights glowing through the windows and someone inside the old, wooden hut.

As Rapp peers through the window, he sees bones hanging from the ceiling, and two women inside: Katherine and Olena – the former immediately looks towards him. He ducks away from the window, trying to hide. After a moment, Katherine is there with a knife at his throat, taking his gun away.

The two women lead him into the hut, where his view is distorted as they sit him down in a chair and Katherine tells him, “You’re just in time for the big show” as she ties his wrists together, all while Olena is holding the gun pointed at him, making jokes about it being a “good sword” and pretending to shoot him. Katherine also reminds Olena she is “at home” and not at the hospital – another interesting development, confirming our suspicions that they are the two elder Yagas.

The tight shots in the cabin mixed with the glowing embers of the fire in the small space really make you feel like you were pulled into that room with Rapp as well, witnessing all of the chaos unfold. Rapp begins to share his theory, which he’s extremely confident in: Pam is Katherine’s daughter, Anna, who is luring Eckert to the woods to have sex with him, and then will kill him at 3:33am. Katherine gives mock approval that he clearly knows everything that is to happen.

Carson and Eckert come upon the cabin, looking through the windows and seeing Rapp tied up inside. Despite Eckert saying he feels fucked up and wants to wait for backup, they burst into the cabin, guns drawn. Following shouting and Eckert demanding Olena lower her gun, Carson shockingly steps over to Olena and Katherine, grabs the gun from Olena, and shoots Eckert in the shoulder.

“I told you to leave it alone. I told you to wait for me at the motel,” Carson says as the camera slowly zooms in on her while she stares directly into Rapp’s eyes across the room. Within seconds, Olena refers to Carson as “Anna” and the shock and confusion on Rapp’s face increases threefold as he realizes who Carson really is.

She is Katherine’s daughter. She is Olena’s granddaughter. She is the third Yaga.

While we as viewers also take in this information, one’s mind goes into a frenzy thinking back on everything we saw with Carson – every little detail that we may have missed. In Episode 7, Katherine says to Carson as she’s leaving her house, “And officer, the last I checked, your job is justice for victims, not helping some billionaire fixer.” That line and so many others now have completely different meanings following this shocking reveal.

Carson knocks out Eckert, and the scene continues unfolding as Carson and Katherine argue about killing Eckert or killing Rapp. We hear Carson saying she wants to give more of the potion to Eckert, that she will have sex with him to get pregnant and have his baby, and will kill him instead of their apparent plan to do so with Rapp. Carson is then speaking in Ukrainian to Olena, trying to convince her of this new plan, saying that Eckert is a bad person and Rapp is much better than him, while Rapp is catching up to the fact that he is supposed to be the one who dies – the third man. The bad dog.

As he’s panicking, Carson tells him to shut up because she’s trying to help him. He says there must be a mistake. “Oh, no mistake,” Olena states simply, while Katherine adds, “No, no, you were chosen.” Rapp asks Carson if she knew, and she responds, looking almost defeated as she says, “not at first.”

As Rapp is grasping all of this in a panic, we find out even more revelations, including that the various young women in town (Olena’s “little witches”) were in on it and helped lay down the clues for Rapp to uncover, including the texts from Henry, the testicles in the cooler, and spiking Rapp’s drink earlier in the night while he was looking through Pam’s room.

And we finally get the answer we’ve been waiting for all along: Katherine killed Henry and Logan, which she proudly admits.

Carson continues arguing to save Rapp’s life and instead kill Eckert, saying that yes, Rapp is an asshole and a fuckboy, but he’s not a “bad dog.” In another shocking twist, Katherine’s response to that is to finally just shoot Eckert and kill him, leaving Carson screaming at her in response. Katherine says defensively that it wouldn’t have worked and they need to proceed as planned.

In response to Carson asking Katherine why they have to kill them, Carrie-Anne Moss delivers her next line flawlessly, saying, “What, take them to court so they can throw the cases out? Henry raped a child. Logan did nothing. Maybe I enjoy knowing these men will never hurt anyone ever again.”

Rapp tells Carson that he loves her, and Katherine pulls Carson to look at her as she tells her, more seriously than ever, that he’s a liar and she herself knows it in her gut. “Yaga is the punisher. Bad dog is the invisible monster, and Yaga is the only one who can see him.” Katherine continues saying, “we are all Yaga, and if you don’t kill him, she ends with you. This is your birthright.”

Carson states that she wants her future daughter to have a choice in the matter, not being forced to be born from having a father who was a terrible person and who is dead. At this point, Rapp is desperately trying to convince them to release him by painting a picture of him helping them go after all the bad dogs, utilizing his years of experience working for the Parks and having dirt on many, many people.

Just when we think he might actually be safe, and Carson might refuse to go through with it all, Rapp tells her he has “the tape” of Henry raping Lily, saying they could use that against the Parks. Carson is immediately suspicious, asking why he has it without her knowledge. He says he took it to expose the truth of what happened. Right away, she knows he’s lying, and she says no – he took it as an insurance policy to protect himself. As this is happening, we see Rapp working at cutting the zip ties from his wrists behind the chair.

Carson looks directly at him and says, “I’m ready” and Katherine comes over to her as they prepare to start the ritual of torture. Rapp is now screaming and begging for them to stop, and right as Carson leans down, about to castrate him, he gets free and knocks her back as he flees out of the cabin.

We see Rapp running through the woods to a clearing on a cliffside near the beach, as Carson finds him – she keeps calm and acts like nothing happened, saying she just found him wandering in the woods. He’s shouting at her about how he knows she’s a witch, yet she’s pretending like she doesn’t know what he’s talking about.

Noah Reid’s acting throughout both of these episodes is phenomenal, especially in this scene, as he’s breaking down and saying he knows he’s a piece of shit, but he wants to be better. He shows his desperation, but also seems to possibly mean what he’s saying. He wants to be a good dog, not a bad dog. He’s sobbing and begging for forgiveness.

Right as he’s about to go to Carson and trust her, he sees Katherine walk up behind her, and he knows it’s a lie. He quickly calls for “The Horns” from a previous fairytale Katherine had shared on the podcast, where a phoenix will come and save a worthy opponent in this situation. He sees a phoenix come towards him in the sky and he jumps off the cliff towards it, despite both women telling him that’s not going to work. Unfortunately, the phoenix does not save him, and he is not freed from being the chosen one for the Yaga’s. He falls and smashes his head on the ground, but he’s still alive.

The next time we see Rapp is the last time, as he’s naked and tied to a tree while Carson lights a fire around him, burning him alive. The three Yagas are then grinding his bones in the mortar and pestle. The episode closes out with Carson telling the Parks what the final decision was on their case – which was, of course, fabricated to put others like Rapp at fault, and free Geena while also exposing what Henry did to Lily. The Parks are unsurprisingly shocked that they are not getting their way. Justice is served.

At the very end, after the screen fades to black, we see Carson having her baby, while speaking about there only being three Yagas at once to make room for the newborn. Olena is in the background and Katherine is holding the baby, and all of a sudden concern flashes across her face when Carson asks to see her – with Katherine responding, “It’s a boy.”

Carson seems shocked, but still looks to be nothing but enamored by her baby boy. From what we now know about this tale of Baba Yaga, there are only daughters, so it will be interesting to see what story develops next in Season 2.

articles.title: Hollow Knight: Silksong Cherry Time! Special Presentation Reveals Expansion Release Date
articles.summary: Hollow Knight: Silksong developer Team Cherry is set to issue a long-awaited update on expansion Sea of Sorrow during a Direct-style special presentation today, and IGN is reporting live.
articles.body:
Hollow Knight: Silksong developer Team Cherry's Cherry Time! Special Presentation wrapped up with a release date for expansion Sea of Sorrow. It's free for all players from December 11.

And if you need a catch up on the presentation, check out our live blog!

I must say, I thought we'd get more than a teaser trailer and a release date for Sea of Sorrow when it comes to Hollow Knight news from this presentation, but perhaps Team Cherry wants to hold back. It said barely anything about the expansion itself, although the trailer did tease new elements.

It was cool to see Team Cherry use its enormous platform to boost three Australian indie devs though. I imagine they're thrilled to have their games put in front of such a huge audience. Good luck to them!

Well, it's time to wrap this live blog up. Thanks for tuning in. See you at the next one!

Sea of Sorrow comes out December 11, Team Cherry has confirmed.

And... that's it! That's all we're getting. A release date announcement and a trailer for the expansion.

Team Cherry is back to thank all the players and fans of the Hollow Knight games. It's now ready to show Sea of Sorrow. "This one is an expansion unlike any we've done before."

And the third game is The Botanist and the Translator, a 2D adventure set on a distant planet. There you try to solve a mystery in a lush world.

The second game is influenced by '80s music. It's called Radio Rain, and looks like a 2D side-scrolling action adventure.

This looks quite nice, actually. Blokkan Secret of the Walking City is the name.

Team Cherry starts by introducing a few new games from fellow Australian developers. One is game that began life as a graphic novel but is now a video game.

While you wait, check out IGN's Hollow Knight: Silksong review , which returned a deserved 9/10.

This one is really hard to call. Team Cherry has promised an update on the Sea of Sorrow DLC for Hollow Knight: Silksong, but it also teased “a bunch of exciting announcements” on top. This developer is hard to predict, so it could be anything from a shadow-drop of Sea of Sorrow to a release date for, perhaps, some time in December. When Sea of Sorrow was announced it was set for 2026, and there's not much left of the year to fit it in.

Or... Team Cherry will say that Sea of Sorrow has grown so big it has evolved into a standalone Hollow Knight game, and it's due out next year or the year after that or the year after that! I'm half joking, but I do hope Team Cherry teases its next game during the presentation. Why do a presentation at all unless you've got something significant to talk about?

Welcome to our live coverage of Tem Cherry's special Hollow Knight: Silkson presentation. We'll have all the news as it happens right here.

Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea of Sorrow Launch Trailer Finally Confirms Release Date, Teases Fishing
articles.summary: Team Cherry's latest showcase gives us a release date for Sea of Sorrow, the free DLC expansion coming to Hollow Knight: Silksong, and a launch trailer.
articles.body:
Team Cherry has just wrapped up its Cherry Time! showcase, giving us some long-awaited news on the future of Hollow Knight: Silksong.

The big takeaway here is that Hollow Knight: Silksong's first big expansion, Sea of Sorrow, finally has a release date of December 11. Sea of Sorrow will be available to all Silksong players for free. All you need is a copy of the base game, and you can start playing Sea of Sorrow when it goes live on December 11.

This also means Team Cherry has stuck to its promise to get Sea of Sorrow out by the end of the year. Some had feared that today's announcement would be a delay — or an announcement that the DLC was being expanded into a full game, which is famously how Silksong's development began.

In the showcase, we got a new look at Sea of Sorrow's gameplay. This gives us a good preview of what's in store for us, as we see new areas, enemies, and boss fights. Of course, it all looks as challenging as ever, as you'd expect for Silksong's post-launch DLC. And is that a fishing mini-game teased at the end?

We weren't told anything else about the future of Silksong or the Hollow Knight series at large. There was no mention of this being Silksong's only expansion, so it's very possible that Team Cherry plans to support the game beyond Sea of Sorrow.

For now, here's the official blurb on Sea of Sorrow:

In Sea of Sorrow, players will voyage above and beneath Pharloom’s forgotten ocean, across islands, through forts and into deep caverns beneath the waves. We’ve spent the whole year stuffing this adventure full with all the things you’d expect from Hollow Knight: Silksong - crazed characters, high adventure, and epic bosses! It’s also overflowing with more exceptional music by the eternally talented Christopher Larkin! We’re pretty darn excited to get it into all of your hands on December 11, so please look forward to it.

Outside of this reveal, Team Cherry used the attention to promote indie games from other studios. Three were shown off: Blokkan: Secret of the Walking City, which is fully hand-drawn; Radio Rain, which is centred around 1980s-inspired music; and The Botanist and the Translator, which boasts a Sailor Moon-esque vibe.

In a follow-up blog post , Team Cherry confirmed that these new games will release under the new Team Cherry Presents label, which is headed up by the indie developer's fourth team member, Huy Le. Huy is technical director and on-going support for all the Team Cherry Presents games, but has also helped out on Silksong and Sea of Sorrow. "As a long-time team of three people, adding a fourth member is a big deal!" Team Cherry said.

Rhiannon (she/her) is a freelance journalist who has been in the industry since 2019. She won MCV's Women in Games award in 2025 and adores RPGs. You can follow her on Bluesky at @rhithewitch.

articles.title: Steam's 2026 Black Friday Sale Brings First-Time Discounts to New PC Games
articles.summary: Steam is getting in on the Black Friday deals, offering thousands of discounted PC games, more than a few of which just released this year.
articles.body:
Steam is getting in on the Black Friday deals , offering thousands of discounted PC games, more than a few of which just released this year. Some, like The Blood of Dawnwalker and Gears of War: E-Day, are seeing their first price cuts ever on Valve's digital games platform. Feel free to peruse the full Steam sale yourself to see what sticks out.

In addition to the games above this sale also covers two great 2026 Star Wars games: Star Wars: Zero Company and Star Wars: Galactic Racer . It also includes Silent Hill: Townfall and Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival , two terrifying and fun first-person horror games. Of those two, Townfall might be the best, at least if you agree with Tristan Ogilvie, who's IGN review gave it an eight and called it "a welcome shot in the arm" for the Silent Hill series.

For something older, I'd recommend Avowed if you enjoy open-world first-person RPGs, as well as The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered , a beautiful update of the 2015 classic. For more of a retro feel, Shinobi: Art of Vengeance is a great reinvention of the series and is also on sale.

There a nice selection of physical games on sale at some of their lowest prices we've seen, with many as low as just $15, seen below.

articles.title: Take the Big Bang Burger Challenge With the Official Persona Cookbook, Now 50% Off
articles.body:
If you’ve ever been enticed by the ridiculous meals in the Persona games, you’re in luck. Atlus partnered with Insight Editions for an official Persona cookbook, collecting 55 recipes from the three most recent games. (Well, remakes.)

The cookbook was released just last year, and has dropped to a new low price in Amazon's Black Friday sale . The discount knocks a whole 50% off the Persona cookbook , bringing the price of Sojiro's coffee secrets down to $14.

The official Persona cookbook collects 55 recipes from the three most recent remakes: Persona 3 Reload, Persona 4 Golden, and Persona 5 Royal. Sorry P1 and P2 fans. I hope Atlus will (finally) be treating you soon enough .

The recipe adaptations come from Jarrett Melendez , the former chef behind a number of video game cookbooks, including an unofficial GTA guide . Each recipe is broken down into allegedly 'easy' steps with descriptions about the in-game lore. And pages are decorated with real photography of each completed meal, as well as illustrations and screenshots from the Persona games .

All 55 recipes appear in some form across the three games, whether as a character’s favorite food, a potential gift, or a meal you can eat for a quick stat boost. Obviously, in-game restaurants like Café Leblanc are heavily featured.

Some of the recipes are slightly spiced up takes on classics, like Shinjiro’s beloved katsudon, while others are a bit extreme in their in-game accuracy. Looking at you, Big Bang Burger Challenge.

We’ll get our next taste of remastered Atlus food with Persona 4 Revival , coming to consoles next year. But I’m sure we’ll get an entirely new feast with the now officially announced Persona 6 .

If you're looking to stock up on random books, Amazon has a massive '3 for 2' sale that also includes vinyl and random craft activities. The Atlus store is also hosting a 'Buy 2 Get 1 Free' sale for Black Friday, but the standalone merch discounts aren't great. Still, it’s worth a scroll.

You’ll find the best 'general' deals at retailers like Amazon and Target, while digital games are on sale through Nintendo , PlayStation , Xbox , and Steam .

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.
